description: BEP publisher, JetStream consumer, event-store, forwarding, and background ingest performance for bep-nats

panels.title: BEP Publish vs Decode Rate
panels.description: Compares only build-tool/progress messages accepted by JetStream with subscriber-decoded Bazel events. Decoded events intentionally exclude stream-control envelopes, so this is not a direct database write-rate comparison. Treat only sustained separation accompanied by Durable Pending / Ack-Pending growth as subscriber backlog.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (stream, le) (rate(hermetiq_bep_queue_latency_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", stream=~"${stream_regex:raw}", delivery_bucket="1"}[5m])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (stream, event_type, le) (rate(hermetiq_bep_process_latency_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", stream=~"${stream_regex:raw}", consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}", consumer_type!="raw_archive", event_type=~"${event_type_regex:raw}"}[5m])))

panels.title: Queue and Process p95
panels.description: p95 first-delivery queue latency from NATS message timestamp to consumer/store handling, plus process latency grouped by stream and event type. Redeliveries and unlabeled legacy samples are excluded from the queue-latency target so this panel reflects healthy-path backlog/freshness.

targets.expr: sum by (project, error_type) (rate(hermetiq_bep_store_total{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", event_type=~"${event_type_regex:raw}", path=~"${path_regex:raw}", status="error"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Error Rate
panels.description: Combined error-rate view for publish failures, consumer processing failures, store failures, DLQ moves, async publish ack errors, and async capacity timeouts. Use this to identify which pipeline stage fails first.

panels.title: Overview
panels.description: Top-level BEP ingest health across the selected filters: JetStream acceptance, subscriber processing, queue/process latency, and broad error rates.

panels.title: Publish Attempts
panels.description: Rate of JetStream publish attempts recorded after publish ack/error, grouped by project, subject, and status. `status="success"` is the canonical accepted-by-JetStream rate.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (project, subject, le) (rate(hermetiq_publish_duration_seconds_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", subject=~"${subject_regex:raw}", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[5m])))

histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (project, subject, le) (rate(hermetiq_publish_duration_seconds_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", subject=~"${subject_regex:raw}", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Publish Duration Percentiles
panels.description: Duration of a single JetStream publish attempt, excluding retry loops. p95 uses a 5m window for stable tails; p50 uses the dashboard rate interval for responsiveness.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (project, subject, le) (rate(hermetiq_publish_request_duration_seconds_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", subject=~"${subject_regex:raw}", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[5m])))

histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (project, subject, le) (rate(hermetiq_publish_request_duration_seconds_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", subject=~"${subject_regex:raw}", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Publish Request Percentiles
panels.description: End-to-end logical publish request duration, including retry time and duplicate-in-progress retry loops. This is broader than Publish Duration and closer to publish-side client delay.

panels.title: Retries and Duplicates
panels.description: JetStream retry and duplicate-ack rates. Retry labels include attempt and error type; duplicate indicates JetStream acknowledged the message ID as already published.

panels.title: Async Inflight by Connection
panels.description: Exact count of application-observed async publishes still awaiting settlement for each physical pod connection under the selected project and subject filters. High values near the per-connection limit indicate local capacity pressure.

panels.title: Async Inflight Total
panels.description: Exact count of application-observed async publishes still awaiting settlement across publisher connections. High values indicate global backlog even if one connection is not saturated.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (project, subject, le) (rate(hermetiq_publish_async_ack_duration_seconds_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", subject=~"${subject_regex:raw}", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[5m])))

histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (project, subject, le) (rate(hermetiq_publish_async_ack_duration_seconds_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", subject=~"${subject_regex:raw}", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: JetStream Publish Settlement Percentiles
panels.description: Time from async JetStream publish enqueue until the application observer records an ack, error, or local safety timeout. Settlement is observed independently of FIFO gRPC response ordering; compare with gRPC Response Percentiles to identify ordering/send delay. Error series can include an unknown outcome when the NATS client never settles a future. Historical samples before this instrumentation change included FIFO observation delay.

panels.title: Async Errors
panels.description: Async JetStream publish future errors by subject and low-cardinality error type. Empty is healthy; nonzero errors mean the future resolved with an ack failure.

targets.expr: sum by (project, subject, publisher_connection) (rate(hermetiq_publish_capacity_total{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", subject=~"${subject_regex:raw}", publisher_connection=~"${publisher_connection_regex:raw}", status="timeout"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Capacity Timeouts
panels.description: Rate of async publisher capacity waits ending in timeout, by publisher connection. Nonzero values mean requests could not enter the async publish window before deadline.

panels.title: Graceful Shutdown Drain State
panels.description: Current publisher drain state used to diagnose gRPC graceful-stop timeouts: active BEP build-tool streams, accepted events being flushed to ordered ACK responses during shutdown, and the exact additive count of async publishes whose application observers have not settled.

panels.title: Received vs Accepted vs Responded Rate
panels.description: End-to-end rate comparison for build_tool stream events. RECEIVED is the ingest SLO: everything Bazel successfully sent that the publisher handled, i.e. outcome publishable OR skipped — a deliberately dropped event was handled, not lost. outcome=error is excluded on purpose so failures cannot masquerade as throughput. DROPPED AT PUBLISHER counts events discarded before NATS (named_set_of_files when the project disables output files, symlink actions, successful actions when the project disables them, empty progress); expect roughly 15% on a typical Bazel profile with output files off. ACCEPTED is what reached JetStream, so received minus dropped should track it. RESPONDED is successful gRPC Send. Divergence between accepted and responded identifies publish stalls; divergence between received and accepted is expected and equals dropped.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (project, subject, le) (rate(hermetiq_publish_grpc_to_js_ack_duration_seconds_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", subject=~"${subject_regex:raw}", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[5m])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (project, subject, le) (rate(hermetiq_publish_grpc_to_js_ack_duration_seconds_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", subject=~"${subject_regex:raw}", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[5m])))

panels.title: gRPC to JetStream Settlement Percentiles
panels.description: Time from successful gRPC Recv until the application observer records an async JetStream ack, error, or local safety timeout for build_tool events. Settlement is observed independently of FIFO response ordering. p95/p99 use 5m windows; compare with gRPC Response Percentiles, but do not subtract aggregate quantiles.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (project, subject, le) (rate(hermetiq_bep_grpc_response_duration_seconds_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", subject=~"${subject_regex:raw}", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[5m])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (project, subject, le) (rate(hermetiq_bep_grpc_response_duration_seconds_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", subject=~"${subject_regex:raw}", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[5m])))

panels.title: gRPC Response Percentiles
panels.description: Client-visible gap from successful gRPC Recv to `req.Send(...)` completion for build_tool events. This includes publish/ack wait plus response ordering and send time.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (project, publisher_connection, subject, le) (rate(hermetiq_publish_capacity_wait_duration_seconds_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", subject=~"${subject_regex:raw}", publisher_connection=~"${publisher_connection_regex:raw}", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[5m])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (project, publisher_connection, subject, le) (rate(hermetiq_publish_capacity_wait_duration_seconds_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", subject=~"${subject_regex:raw}", publisher_connection=~"${publisher_connection_regex:raw}", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[5m])))

panels.title: Capacity Wait Percentiles
panels.description: Time spent waiting for async JetStream publish capacity before enqueue. High tails or timeout status indicate local async window or max-pending pressure.

panels.title: Direct Invocation Start Outcomes
panels.description: Publisher direct-to-DB invocation-start rate by outcome. `created` is the true new-invocations-per-second rate; `conflict` is an idempotent duplicate. `timeout`, `error`, `canceled`, and `saturated` fall back to JetStream.

panels.title: Direct Invocation Start SQL Latency
panels.description: Publisher-side latency of actual direct invocation-start SQL attempts. Saturated requests are excluded because they never enter the database; correlate latency errors with the outcome-rate panel to see JetStream fallbacks.

panels.title: Publisher
panels.description: Publisher-side view of Bazel gRPC event ingest, direct invocation-start SQL writes, and JetStream publish behavior before subscribers consume events.

panels.title: Fetch Rate
panels.description: Rate of JetStream pull consumer Fetch calls by consumer type and status. Drops or errors here indicate consumers are not pulling batches normally.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (consumer_type, le) (rate(hermetiq_consumer_fetch_duration_seconds_bucket{consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}", consumer_type!="raw_archive", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[5m])))

panels.title: Fetch Request Duration Percentiles
panels.description: Duration of the JetStream Fetch call that creates an asynchronous MessageBatch. This does not include waiting for that batch's message channel to fill or expire; that delivery wait is included in Batch Drain and Dispatch Duration.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (consumer_type, le) (rate(hermetiq_consumer_batch_duration_seconds_bucket{consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}", consumer_type!="raw_archive", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[5m])))

panels.title: Batch Drain and Dispatch Duration
panels.description: On the pipelined path, time spent draining the asynchronous JetStream MessageBatch channel, parsing messages, and dispatching worker shards. It includes waiting until the pull fills or expires but excludes worker store/ACK time; a high value with low pod CPU can therefore mean delivery starvation rather than parser saturation.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (consumer_type, le) (rate(hermetiq_consumer_batch_messages_bucket{consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}", consumer_type!="raw_archive", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[5m])))

panels.title: Batch Size Percentiles
panels.description: Distribution of message counts returned in each consumer batch. Low batch size during high load can indicate fetch limits, partition skew, or insufficient available messages.

targets.expr: sum by (consumer_type, action, status) (rate(hermetiq_consumer_ack_total{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}", consumer_type!="raw_archive", event_type=~"${event_type_regex:raw}", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: ACK / NAK Rate
panels.description: Rate of consumer ACK/NAK operations by action and status. `nak_delay` and `ack_dlq` reveal retry/DLQ behavior; ack errors mean JetStream did not confirm the consumer action.

targets.expr: max by (consumer_type, stream, consumer, state) (hermetiq_consumer_state{consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}", consumer_type!="raw_archive", stream=~"${stream_regex:raw}", state=~"num_pending|num_ack_pending"})

panels.title: Durable Pending / Ack-Pending
panels.description: Current per-durable JetStream backlog, split by consumer kind and de-duplicated across pods reporting the same consumer. NumPending is filter-matching messages not yet delivered; NumAckPending is delivered but unsettled. These two states are the authoritative current backlog signals.

panels.title: Fetch Calls vs Settled Messages
panels.description: Compares pull fetch-call rate with successful terminal ACK actions, including blob-progress ack-on-buffer, ignored nil payloads, and DLQ settlement. A large lifecycle gap can be deliberate low-latency polling/empty fetch churn; use Pending/Ack-Pending for backlog.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (stream, le) (rate(hermetiq_bep_queue_latency_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", stream=~"${stream_regex:raw}", stream=~".*LIFECYCLE.*", delivery_bucket="1"}[15m])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (stream, le) (rate(hermetiq_bep_queue_latency_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", stream=~"${stream_regex:raw}", stream=~".*LIFECYCLE.*", delivery_bucket="1"}[15m])))

panels.title: Lifecycle Queue Tail (15m)
panels.description: Lifecycle-only first-delivery queue latency over a 15m rolling window. Redeliveries and unlabeled legacy samples are excluded so this stays focused on user-visible start freshness.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (stream, le) (rate(hermetiq_bep_queue_latency_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", stream=~"${stream_regex:raw}", stream=~".*BUILD_TOOL.*", delivery_bucket="1"}[15m])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (stream, le) (rate(hermetiq_bep_queue_latency_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", stream=~"${stream_regex:raw}", stream=~".*BUILD_TOOL.*", delivery_bucket="1"}[15m])))

panels.title: Build-Tool / Progress Queue Tail (15m)
panels.description: Build-tool/progress first-delivery queue latency over a 15m rolling window. Redeliveries and unlabeled legacy samples are excluded so this panel reflects healthy-path backlog/freshness.

panels.title: Lifecycle Start Wait Outcomes
panels.description: Rate of build-tool/progress batches that waited for lifecycle-start visibility, grouped by outcome and message-count bucket. Spikes here explain invocation_start_time_unavailable retry pressure.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (project, consumer_type, outcome, le) (rate(hermetiq_consumer_lifecycle_start_wait_duration_seconds_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}"}[5m])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (project, consumer_type, outcome, le) (rate(hermetiq_consumer_lifecycle_start_wait_duration_seconds_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}"}[5m])))

panels.title: Lifecycle Start Wait Duration
panels.description: Tail duration spent waiting for lifecycle-start visibility before retrying build-tool/progress events in memory.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (consumer_type, message_count_bucket, le) (rate(hermetiq_consumer_worker_batch_duration_seconds_bucket{consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}", consumer_type!="raw_archive"}[5m])))

panels.title: Worker Batch Duration
panels.description: Duration to store and ACK one in-process worker shard, grouped by consumer type and batch-size bucket. Use this when queue latency rises without matching store-duration movement.

panels.title: Worker Queue Depth
panels.description: Per-worker pipeline queue depth (max across pods). One worker pinned high while its siblings sit near zero is the noisy-invocation signature: that invocation is concentrated on its hash-affine worker while the rest of the pipeline keeps flowing.

panels.title: Pipeline Queued Messages
panels.description: Messages held by the worker pipeline per durable (queued plus in-process). The hottest pod approaching pipelineMaxQueuedMessages (default 2x batchSize) means dispatch is backpressuring fetch — either the DB is slow or one worker owns a sustained backlog.

panels.title: Pipeline Queued Bytes
panels.description: Payload bytes held by the worker pipeline per durable, bounding subscriber-pod memory. The hottest pod approaching pipelineMaxQueuedBytes (default 2x maxRequestMaxBytes, or 128MiB) means the byte budget, not the message budget, is gating fetch-ahead.

panels.title: Queue Residence Percentiles
panels.description: Time a message waits in its worker queue between enqueue and dequeue. It must stay well below the durable's configured AckWait; residence approaching AckWait precedes lease expiry. Cross-check current NumAckPending first, then Current Redelivery Pressure for evidence of repeated deliveries.

targets.expr: sum by (consumer_type) (max by (consumer_type, stream, consumer) (hermetiq_consumer_state{consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}", consumer_type!="raw_archive", stream=~"${stream_regex:raw}", state="num_pending"}))

sum by (consumer_type) (max by (consumer_type, stream, consumer) (hermetiq_consumer_state{consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}", consumer_type!="raw_archive", stream=~"${stream_regex:raw}", state="num_ack_pending"}))

panels.title: Fleet Backlog by Durable Kind
panels.description: Fleet totals for current NumPending and NumAckPending after taking one value per durable consumer. This prevents shared consumer state reported by multiple subscriber replicas from being counted more than once.

targets.expr: topk(12, max by (consumer_type, stream, consumer) (hermetiq_consumer_state{consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}", consumer_type!="raw_archive", stream=~"${stream_regex:raw}", state="num_redelivered"}))

panels.title: Current Redelivery Pressure
panels.description: Top durable consumers by JetStream NumRedelivered: messages currently in redelivery state and not yet acknowledged. Each message is counted once while unsettled, so this value can fall as messages are acknowledged. It does not expose whether NAK, AckWait expiry, pod loss, or connection loss caused the redelivery.

targets.expr: topk(12, max by (consumer_type, stream, consumer) (hermetiq_consumer_state{consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}", consumer_type!="raw_archive", stream=~"${stream_regex:raw}", state="consumer_lag"}))

panels.title: ACK-Floor Sequence Gap (Diagnostic Only)
panels.description: Delivered consumer sequence minus ACK-floor sequence. This is not a message backlog count: one old unsettled delivery can hold the ACK floor behind many already-settled later messages. Correlate it with that durable's NumAckPending.

panels.title: Dispatcher-Held vs Worker Pipeline
panels.description: Fetched messages in the dispatcher tail were previously invisible: JetStream counted them as ACK-pending, but the pipeline queued gauge began only after worker enqueue. A large dispatcher-held tail with low worker depth localizes the missing lease time before worker ownership.

panels.title: Lease Renewal Outcomes
panels.description: InProgress outcomes by bounded scope: dispatcher_held, worker_dequeue, coalescer_wait, coalescer_pre_store, and missing_start. Any sustained error series directly explains silent AckWait expiry; high success volume identifies where messages are spending their lease.

targets.expr: max by (consumer_type) (hermetiq_consumer_ack_deadline_seconds{consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}"}) - on (consumer_type) histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (consumer_type, le) (rate(hermetiq_consumer_lease_disposition_age_seconds_bucket{consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}"}[5m])))

panels.title: Lease Age and Deadline Headroom
panels.description: Age since the most recent successful delivery or InProgress renewal when ownership finishes. First deliveries are sampled 1/64; every redelivery is retained. Headroom at or below zero means the p99 disposition reached the effective BackOff[0]/AckWait deadline.

panels.title: Delivery-to-Disposition Age
panels.description: Total local ownership age through ACK, delayed NAK, skip, or shutdown abandonment. Compare this with lease age: a high delivery age with low lease age proves renewals are successfully protecting long-lived work.

panels.title: Deadline Exceeded and Expired Copies
panels.description: Observed delivery attempts 2+ overlaid with sampled dispositions at or beyond the effective deadline and unsampled local expired-copy skips. Expired copies directly confirm AckWait expiry; a remaining gap is server-side or process-loss redelivery that the application could not observe at the prior disposition.

panels.title: Server-Confirmed ACK Sample Rate
panels.description: JetStream DoubleAck samples confirmed by the consumer leader: 1/1024 of first deliveries and 1/128 of redeliveries, selected deterministically by stream sequence. An error means confirmation was not received, not that the ACK was necessarily unapplied; correlate errors with route/leader health and durable deletion or recreation.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (consumer_type, event_type, status, le) (rate(hermetiq_consumer_ack_confirmation_duration_seconds_bucket{consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}"}[5m])))

panels.title: Server-Confirmed ACK Latency p95
panels.description: Round-trip time from the subscriber through NATS to the durable consumer leader for the bounded DoubleAck sample. Rising latency before redeliveries while local disposition age remains low implicates the ACK route; confirmation errors can also mean a replaced durable generation or a lost/late reply.

panels.title: Consumers
panels.description: JetStream pull consumer health: fetch calls, batch processing, ACK/NAK operations, de-duplicated backlog, lifecycle-start freshness, queue tails split by stream class, worker-pipeline fetch-ahead, dispatcher-held deliveries, acknowledgement lease renewal/expiry diagnostics, and sampled consumer-leader ACK confirmation.

targets.expr: sum by (project, path, event_type, status) (rate(hermetiq_bep_store_total{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", path=~"${path_regex:raw}", event_type=~"${event_type_regex:raw}", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Store Operation Rate
panels.description: Rate of event-store operations by path, BEP event type, project, and status. Paths distinguish single writes, deferred single writes, bulk writes, and bulk fallbacks.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (path, event_type, le) (rate(hermetiq_bep_store_duration_seconds_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", path=~"${path_regex:raw}", event_type=~"${event_type_regex:raw}", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[5m])))

histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (path, event_type, le) (rate(hermetiq_bep_store_duration_seconds_bucket{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", path=~"${path_regex:raw}", event_type=~"${event_type_regex:raw}", status=~"${status_regex:raw}"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Store Duration Percentiles
panels.description: Duration of event-store operations by write path and event type. Use with Store Operation Rate to separate frequent write paths from slow ones.

panels.title: Bulk Flush Rows and Fallbacks
panels.description: Bulk SQL flush throughput and fallback count by event type. Fallbacks mean a bulk write failed and the store attempted per-row writes instead.

panels.title: Bulk Flush Duration Percentiles
panels.description: Duration of bulk SQL flushes by event type. Tail spikes here identify database batch commit/write latency, separate from per-event store duration.

panels.title: BuildMetrics Outcomes
panels.description: BuildMetrics persistence outcomes by project. Result labels show whether BuildMetrics payloads were inserted, skipped, or errored.

panels.title: BuildMetrics Duration
panels.description: Duration of BuildMetrics persistence by project and result. Result labels show inserted, skipped, or error outcomes.

panels.title: Final Build-Tool Event to DB Lag Percentiles
panels.description: Lag from Bazel client timestamp on the final build_tool BuildFinished event to the successful invocation DB update. Use as a proxy for final-event end-to-DB visibility.

For each project over the dashboard range: `started` = build_tool started events, `final event` = finished events the subscriber saw, `final DB update` = finished events successfully persisted, and `missing final` = started minus finished, clamped to 0.

targets.expr: (sum by (project) (increase(hermetiq_bep_final_build_tool_event_db_lag_duration_seconds_count{project=~"${project_regex:raw}"}[$__range])) or on(project) 0 * sum by (project) (increase(hermetiq_events_total{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", event_type="started"}[$__range])))

clamp_min(sum by (project) (increase(hermetiq_events_total{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", event_type="started"}[$__range])) - (sum by (project) (increase(hermetiq_events_total{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", event_type="finished"}[$__range])) or on(project) 0 * sum by (project) (increase(hermetiq_events_total{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", event_type="started"}[$__range]))), 0)

panels.title: Build-Tool Invocation Finality Counts

panels.description: Committed and ACKed build_tool messages over the selected dashboard range, grouped by project and decoded Bazel BuildEvent payload type.

targets.expr: sort_desc(sum by (project, bazel_event_type) (increase(hermetiq_consumer_ack_total{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}", event_type="build_tool", action="ack", status="success"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Build-Tool Event Type Counts

panels.description: BES upload lag per project: attempt_finish_time (lifecycle InvocationAttemptFinished, emitted after the BES upload drains) minus finish_time (BuildFinished, the actual build end). Measures how long Bazel clients wait on BEP upload after the build completes.
panels.title: BES Upload Lag Percentiles
Coalesced Store Batch Size
panels.description: Events per coalesced StoreEvents call — the SQL density the coalescer exists to create. Healthy is near the delivered pull size up to storeBatchMaxEvents; worker-shard-sized values mean no cross-worker coalescing is happening (check Batch Requests).

panels.title: Coalesced Store Batch Requests
panels.description: Complete worker requests combined per store call — p50 above 1 proves cross-worker coalescing. Flushes/s by reason shows whether the event cap or the age cap drives flushing; non-success covers panic and result_mismatch outcomes and should be flat zero.

panels.title: Coalesced Store Batch Wait
panels.description: Age of the oldest worker request when its store call begins, including time queued for a flush lane. Sustained growth means the lanes are saturated: raise storeBatchParallelism or lower storeBatchMaxEvents.

panels.title: Coalesced Store Batch Duration
panels.description: Duration of the coalesced StoreEvents call. Read together with Batch Size: duration scaling linearly with events means per-row cost dominates at this batch size and bigger batches buy nothing — prefer more lanes over a higher event cap.

panels.title: Store and Persistence
panels.description: Database persistence health for BEP events, bulk write paths, BuildMetrics, build_tool payload mix, and final build_tool event lag.

panels.title: Consume Errors
panels.description: Consumer processing errors before final recovery handling, grouped by project, event type, and low-cardinality error type. These typically precede retries or DLQ moves.

panels.title: DLQ and FK Errors
panels.description: Foreign-key dependency errors and DLQ moves. FK errors often mean build_tool child rows arrived before prerequisite rows; DLQ means max deliveries were exhausted and the event was parked.

targets.expr: sum by (project, consumer_type, mechanism, reason, delivery_bucket, status) (rate(hermetiq_consumer_redelivery_trigger_total{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}", consumer_type!="raw_archive", event_type=~"${event_type_regex:raw}"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Application Redelivery Triggers
panels.description: Application paths that explicitly NAK/NakWithDelay or knowingly leave a delivery unacked, grouped by exact local reason. status=error means the NAK call itself failed. This cannot include a pod crash, lost connection, or other server-only cause because the process cannot report what it did not observe.

panels.title: Async Drops
panels.description: Dropped in-process async enrichment jobs, such as background work queues that were full. These are not JetStream publish drops.

panels.title: Failed Operations
panels.description: Failed operational actions across consumer ACK/NAK, Fetch, and event-store writes. Good first stop when broad Error Rate is too aggregated.

targets.expr: sum by (project, consumer_type, event_type, delivery_bucket) (rate(hermetiq_consumer_redelivery_observed_total{project=~"${project_regex:raw}", consumer_type=~"${consumer_type_regex:raw}", consumer_type!="raw_archive", event_type=~"${event_type_regex:raw}"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Observed Redelivery Attempts
panels.description: Actual second-or-later delivery attempts observed by the BEP consumer. This counts attempts, not unique messages. Compare it with Application Redelivery Triggers: any excess is server-unattributed and may be AckWait expiry, pod loss, connection loss, or another path that could not emit a trigger before disappearing.

panels.title: Errors and Recovery
panels.description: Failure paths that determine whether messages retry, enter the DLQ, or drop async background work.

panels.title: Log Compression Outcomes
panels.description: Log compression operation outcomes by trigger source and status. Sources include finish-triggered, ticker, or consumer paths where present.

panels.title: Log Compression Duration
panels.description: Duration of completed log compression attempts by source. Queueing and noop outcomes may appear in the outcome count without duration samples.

panels.title: Progress Chunk Writer Depth
panels.description: Blob-progress records and invocation buffers currently held in memory, plus sealed chunks queued for upload. Progress messages are ACKed when buffered, so these gauges—not progress durable AckPending—show whether the asynchronous writer is accumulating work.

panels.title: Progress Chunk Buffered Bytes
panels.description: Unsealed blob-progress payload bytes in memory, fleet total and hottest pod. Compare the hottest pod with PROGRESS_BLOB_BUFFER_MAX_BYTES; sustained pressure near the cap should coincide with dropped flush outcomes.

panels.title: Progress Chunk Flush Outcomes
panels.description: Sealed progress chunks by outcome: uploaded is healthy; spilled means blob upload failed and records fell back to PostgreSQL; failed means both paths failed; dropped means best-effort shedding because buffer/queue/shutdown capacity was exhausted.

panels.title: Progress Chunk Flush Duration
panels.description: Duration of asynchronous blob upload or fallback handling by outcome. Blob I/O is intentionally off the JetStream ACK path, so increasing duration matters when upload queue depth, buffered bytes, or spill/drop outcomes rise with it.

panels.title: Background Work
panels.description: Background work outside the main event write path, including legacy log-compression signals and the asynchronous blob-backed progress chunk writer.

panels.title: DB Partition Future Coverage
panels.description: Future partition coverage per table in days, computed from the latest child partition upper bound minus monitor time. The threshold series comes from `DB_PARTITION_MONITOR_MIN_FUTURE_COVERAGE`.

panels.title: DB Partition Future Partitions
panels.description: Count of child partitions whose lower bound is in the future, by database and parent table. Drops toward zero mean premake maintenance is falling behind.

panels.title: Aged-Out DB Partitions
panels.description: Partitions older than retention plus grace that still exist, by database and parent table. Nonzero means partition cleanup failed or is delayed.

panels.title: Oldest Aged-Out Partition Overdue
panels.description: How long the oldest undeleted aged-out partition is overdue beyond retention plus grace, in hours. Zero means no aged-out partitions remain.

panels.title: DB Partition Health
panels.description: Database-wide partition maintenance health. These metrics have database/table labels rather than project labels because partitions are shared infrastructure.

panels.title: Queue Latency Heatmap
panels.description: Raw first-delivery queue-latency histogram buckets. Redeliveries and unlabeled legacy samples are excluded so this heatmap reflects healthy-path queue age.

panels.title: Process Latency Heatmap
panels.description: Raw process-latency histogram buckets for selected streams and event types. Useful when p95 is unstable and you need to see where observations land.

panels.title: Publish Duration Heatmap
panels.description: Raw JetStream publish-duration histogram buckets for selected subjects and statuses. This shows single publish-attempt latency distribution.

panels.title: Consumer Batch Duration Heatmap
panels.description: Raw consumer batch-duration histogram buckets. Use this to verify whether batch p95 comes from a broad tail or a small number of high-bucket samples.

panels.title: Store Duration Heatmap
panels.description: Raw event-store duration histogram buckets for selected write paths and event types. Useful for distinguishing DB write tail shape from quantile artifacts.

Distribution of outgoing NATS message sizes, recorded once per message before any retry. Use it with JetStream Publish Settlement Percentiles to test whether a heavy payload tail correlates with higher replication latency.
panels.title: Publish Payload Size Heatmap

panels.description: Payload size split by subject kind, so build_tool can be compared directly against progress on the same partition. Grouped by subject only so the comparison stays readable. p99/p95 use a 5m window for stable tails; p50 uses the dashboard rate interval.
panels.title: Publish Payload Size Percentiles by Subject
Histograms
panels.description: Raw histogram bucket views for latency distributions. Use these when quantiles look unstable or when checking bucket saturation.
